title: Tri-SDK 'Auth Sherpa' and Pullstream Simplifier — unify lightweight token flow and simplified async iterators
author: Marina Kovacs
release_notes: Introduces 'Auth Sherpa' token flow and a simplified pullstream helper for Python/TS/Go SDKs. Backwards-compatible adapter included for older iterator shapes.
description:
Context: multiple SDK teams have been incrementally adding ad-hoc token refresh logic and stream helpers which diverged across languages. This PR introduces a small, opinionated coordination layer we call 'Auth Sherpa' plus a lightweight Pullstream Simplifier that unifies the consumer-facing async iterator/pullstream ergonomics across Python, TypeScript, and Go. Goals: 1) Make refresh behavior consistent (single refresh inflight per session, cooperative backoff), 2) Provide a minimal ergonomic async iterator for common streaming use-cases (resume, abort, graceful drain), 3) Keep adapters for existing SDK shapes so existing callers are not forced to migrate immediately. What changed: consolidated token lifecycle (refresh locks, deduped inflight refresh, soft-ttl hints), added a tiny pullstream helper with a single async iterator primitive and a compact backpressure signal, updated SDK public surfaces with small opt-in flags. Checklist:
- [x] Design doc posted (ENG-9123)
- [x] Implement core SHERPA token orchestrator in each SDK
- [x] Add Pullstream Simplifier helpers and tests
- [x] Add adapters to map old iterator shapes to new surface
- [x] End-to-end smoke tests across hosted API and dedicated endpoints
Notes: this is intentionally conservative. The Sherpa orchestrator exposes a minimal interface: getToken(), invalidate(), and leaseHint(ms). The orchestrator handles single-flight refresh and exposes telemetry hooks. Pullstream Simplifier focuses on consumer ergonomics (async iterator + cancel token + resume checkpoint).
